text: Employee Leave and Attendance Policy Document ID: EN-POL-02 Department: Human Resources Version: 5.0 Effective Date: 1 January 2026 Review Cycle: Annual 1. Purpose This policy sets out the entitlements, procedures, and responsibilities relating to employee leave and attendance at Meridian Holdings Group, ensuring consistent and fair treatment across all departments. 2. Scope This policy applies to all permanent, full-time, and part-time employees. Entitlements for contractors and temporary staff are governed separately by the terms of their individual engagement contracts. 3. Annual Leave 3.1 Full-time employees accrue twenty-five working days of paid annual leave per calendar year, in addition to public holidays observed in the employee's country of employment. 3.2 Annual leave accrues on a pro-rata basis for employees who join or leave the Company partway through the calendar year. 3.3 A maximum of five unused annual leave days may be carried over into the following calendar year, subject to line manager approval. Sick Leave 4.1 Employees are entitled to fourteen days of paid sick leave per calendar year. Purpose This policy sets out Meridian Holdings Group's zero-tolerance approach to bribery and corruption in all its business dealings, wherever the Company operates. 2. title: IT Helpdesk Standard Operating Procedures Manual
text: IT Helpdesk Standard Operating Procedures Manual Document ID: EN-MAN-06 Department: Information Technology Version: 2.5 Effective Date: 1 June 2026 1. Purpose This manual defines the standard procedures followed by the IT Service Desk in logging, prioritising, and resolving employee IT support requests. 2. Ticket Logging 2.1 All support requests must be logged as a ticket in the IT Service Management (ITSM) system, whether received by phone, email, or the self-service portal, including a description of the issue and the affected system. 2.2 Tickets must be categorised at logging using the standard taxonomy: Hardware, Software, Network, Account Access, or Security. 3. Priority Classification 3.1 Tickets are classified into four priority levels: Critical (complete service outage affecting multiple users), High (significant impact on a single user's ability to work), Medium (inconvenience with a workaround available), and Low (minor issue or general request). 3.2 Target response times are: Critical — 15 minutes; High — 1 hour; Medium — 4 hours; Low — 1 working day. Target resolution times are set out in Appendix A. 4. Escalation 4.1 Tickets not resolved within the target

title: Warehouse Inventory Management Manual
text: Warehouse Inventory Management Manual Document ID: EN-MAN-05 Department: Supply Chain and Logistics Version: 3.3 Effective Date: 1 March 2026 1. Purpose This manual describes the standard procedures for receiving, storing, counting, and dispatching inventory at Meridian Holdings Group's distribution centres, to ensure inventory accuracy and operational efficiency. 2. Goods Receipt 2.1 All incoming deliveries must be checked against the corresponding Purchase Order before acceptance, verifying item description, quantity, and condition. 2.2 Discrepancies between the delivery and the Purchase Order must be recorded on a Goods Receipt Discrepancy Form (SCM-FORM-02) and reported to the Procurement Department within one working day. 2.3 Received goods must be scanned into the Warehouse Management System (WMS) at the point of receipt, generating a unique putaway task for warehouse staff. 3. Storage and Location Management 3.1 Items must be stored only in their assigned WMS bin location. title: Forklift Operator Training Manual
text: Forklift Operator Training Manual Document ID: EN-MAN-03 Department: Health, Safety and Environment Version: 1.8 Effective Date: 1 May 2026 1. Purpose This manual sets out the mandatory training curriculum and competency requirements for employees seeking authorisation to operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts) at any Meridian Holdings Group site. 2. Prerequisites 2.1 Candidates must be at least eighteen years of age, hold a valid Company employee ID, and have completed the general Warehouse Health and Safety Induction before beginning forklift-specific training. 2.2 Candidates must pass a basic vision and physical fitness assessment administered by an approved occupational health provider. 3. Training Structure 3.1 Training consists of three stages: theoretical instruction (one full day), supervised practical operation (minimum sixteen hours across five working days), and a final competency assessment. 3.2 Theoretical instruction covers: forklift stability principles and the load centre concept, pre-operation inspection checklists, site-specific traffic rules, and relevant sections of the Workplace Health and Safety Manual (EN-MAN-01). 4. text: Workplace Health and Safety Manual (Warehouse Operations) Document ID: EN-MAN-01 Department: Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Version: 2.4 Effective Date: 1 April 2026 Applicable Sites: Distribution Centres 1–4 1. Introduction This manual sets out the mandatory safety procedures for all personnel working in or visiting Meridian Holdings Group's distribution centres. All employees, contractors, and visitors must complete a site safety induction before entering operational areas. 2. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) 2.1 High-visibility vests must be worn at all times within marked operational zones. 2.2 Steel-toe safety footwear is mandatory for all personnel working on the warehouse floor, including visitors on guided tours. 2.3 Hearing protection must be worn in areas marked with high-noise signage, typically near packing and conveyor machinery. 2.4 Employees operating forklifts or pallet jacks must wear the full PPE set specified in Appendix A, including a hard hat where overhead racking exceeds four metres. 3. title: Workplace Health and Safety Manual
text: 3.1 Employees must not lift loads exceeding 25 kg without mechanical assistance or a second person. 3.2 The correct lifting technique — bending at the knees, keeping the back straight, and holding the load close to the body — must be followed for all manual lifts, as demonstrated during induction training. 3.3 Repetitive lifting tasks are subject to job rotation every two hours to reduce the risk of musculoskeletal injury. 1 4. Fire Safety 4.1 Fire extinguishers are located at intervals of no more than thirty metres throughout the warehouse floor and are colour-coded by type: red (water), blue (dry powder), and black (CO2). 4.2 In the event of a fire alarm, all personnel must proceed immediately to the designated assembly point shown on the site evacuation map, without collecting personal belongings. 4.3 Fire drills are conducted quarterly. text: Forklift and Vehicle Operations 5.1 Only personnel holding a valid, in-date forklift operating licence issued by the Company's approved training provider may operate powered industrial trucks. 5.2 A maximum speed of 8 km/h applies to all forklift movement within the warehouse, reduced to walking pace within two metres of pedestrian walkways. 5.3 Pedestrians have right of way at all marked crossing points. Forklift operators must sound the horn when approaching blind corners or intersections. 6. text: Customer Complaint Handling Manual Document ID: EN-MAN-04 Department: Customer Service Version: 2.1 Effective Date: 1 February 2026 1. Purpose This manual provides Customer Service staff with a consistent process for receiving, investigating, and resolving customer complaints in a fair and timely manner. 2.
